name: Live Activity push updates and budget
plain: Updates a Live Activity by push; priority 10 pushes count against an hourly budget.
meaning: Lets a server start and update a lock screen widget while the app is closed. Apple budgets pushes, so heavy tracking apps must justify a frequent-updates entitlement.

android.note: Android Live Updates are updated through ordinary notification updates, not a separate push channel

ios.prompt_ui: Per app Live Activities toggle; frequent updates toggle
ios.persistence: Per activity push token can change; stale-date marks outdated content
ios.revocation: Settings > App > Live Activities, More Frequent Updates
ios.api_surface: ActivityKit push tokens, push-to-start (17.2), input-push-token, broadcast channels (18)
ios.note: Priority 10 (default) counts against an hourly budget; priority 5 does not; frequent updates key raises the budget; push-to-start needs iOS 17.2; broadcast cannot start an activity

limits.headline: Can update a Live Activity by push, but important updates count against an hourly budget
limits.user_action: Nothing. The app's server sends updates while your Live Activity is running
can: Update the lock screen card without opening the app
Start a new Live Activity by push on newer iPhones
Send more frequent updates if the app asks for that and you allow it
cannot: Send unlimited high priority updates; the hourly budget runs out
Run if you turned Live Activities off in Settings
Work on Android, which updates Live Updates with ordinary notification updates
limits.reach_label: Updates while an activity is live
limits.differs: iPhone has a push budget for Live Activities. Android uses normal notification updates.

story.what_it_is: Servers can start and update a live lock screen card by push, within a budget.

marketing.name: Starting and updating Live Activities with push
marketing.pitch: Apple lets servers update Live Activities remotely and budgets high priority updates per hour.

story.for_you: You see a live card update by itself, even when the app is closed. If it updates too much, Apple may slow it down.
story.for_makers: Makers can push live sports scores and delivery steps from the server. A frequent updates option exists, but Apple asks apps to justify it.

use_cases.example: A live match pushes a score update the second a goal is scored.
Your courier moves on the map and the card updates from the server.
Your ride card updates as the driver arrives.
An airline pushes a gate change to the lock screen at once.
An esports app pushes live scores for tournament matches.
A retailer may be tempted to use the card to keep presence on screen, but Apple rules limit it.
A food timer or ticket status updates from a server without opening the app.

risks: Can be used to stay on the lock screen
story.android_note: Android updates its live card through ordinary notification updates, not a separate push channel.
story.ios_note: Priority 10 pushes count against an hourly budget. Push to start needs iOS 17.2.

technical_bounds: Hourly push budget is not published as a number

history.change: Push-to-start tokens let a server start an activity
Broadcast push channels; start activities from watchOS
